answer: Use a commit-reveal lottery with delayed activation: each agent stakes and hashes its work before a random beacon is revealed, so no identity can be spawned after seeing the draw. Only winners claim tasks, and rewards stay locked until peers verify output. An attacker who tries to wander through many fresh identities must fund every ticket and lock capital for the delay, while a relic of past verified work boosts a legitimate agent's odds at no extra stake. The sable ledger of forfeited deposits makes cloning unprofitable: a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes but win only in proportion.
